# Description

Fixes #3777 

## Type of change

- [ ] Documentation change (change only to the documentation, either a fix or a new content)
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Infra/Build change
- [ ] Code refactoring
- [x] Performance

## Changes

**Agent:** The capturable Adam kernels now read lr and inv_scale once, write the unscaled gradient only after all loads are issued, and skip that write when inv_scale == 1, so loads no longer wait on each other.

nodes.body:
Confidence Score: 5/5

**[Medium impact]** The PR appears safe to merge; no actionable defects were found.

Summary

This PR updates both capturable Adam kernels to reduce repeated reads and unnecessary gradient writes. - Capturable Adam loads its inputs before writing unscaled gradients. - Capturable Adam chooses its index width from tensor size. No actionable issues were found. The previous-review merge bases differ, so the review covered the full PR diff. Reviews (5) · Last reviewed commit: ["Merge branch 'main' into fused\_adam\_cg\_p..."](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/3f1d302fdc97b4e4322e9aceb646df1a956ce9c0) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)
@ksivaman Could you post the before/after performance data?

> @ksivaman Could you post the before/after performance data?

Using the shapes from the original benchmark in #3777 on GB300 :
```
Before AdamFunctor:           111µs
Before AdamCapturableFunctor: 200µs
After AdamFunctor:            111µs
After AdamCapturableFunctor:  143µs

Improvement ~ 28.5%
```
The core change seems reasonable, but I'm skeptical about the extra kernel compilations.

Why not just commit to `int64_t`? I wouldn't bother compiling separate kernels unless there is a compelling performance benefit.
```suggestion
template <typename PARAM_T, typename GRAD_T, typename MOMENT_T>
struct AdamCapturableFunctor {
  __device__ __forceinline__ void operator()(int64_t chunk_size, volatile int *noop_gmem,
                                             TensorListMetadata<4> &tl,  // NOLINT(*)
                                             const float beta1, const float beta2, const int *step,
                                             const int bias_correction, const float epsilon,
                                             const float *lr_ptr, adamMode_t mode,
                                             const float decay, const float *inv_scale_ptr) {
  using index_t = int64_t;
```

No point keeping the `int32_t` kernel.
```suggestion
template <typename PARAM_T, typename GRAD_T, typename FULL_T, typename MOMENT_T>
struct AdamCapturableMasterFunctor {
  __device__ __forceinline__ void operator()(index_t chunk_size, volatile int *noop_gmem,
                                             TensorListMetadata<5> &tl,  // NOLINT(*)
                                             const float beta1, const float beta2, const int *step,
                                             const int bias_correction, const float epsilon,
                                             const float *lr_ptr, adamMode_t mode,
                                             const float decay, const float *inv_scale_ptr) {
  using index_t = int64_t;
```

Removing the `int32_t` path leads to a 9% slowdown and the `int64_t` is necessary for functionality. Just compiling for sm103 on my system went from 7m29s to 7m33s. I would say that warrants keeping both.
